docs.title: Tar Pits
docs.oneLine: Tar as an entrapment hazard, stratified archaeology dig site, controllable fluid weapon, and creature-inhabited fuel economy across the desert world.

rows.section: 2. Tar as terrain — the base state
rows.label: Entrapment and rescue
rows.does: Stepping on tar can trap and slowly drown a pawn; mechs corrode instead; a failed rescue drags the rescuer in too.

rows.section: 2. Tar as terrain — the base state
rows.label: Visible sinking descent
rows.does: Past a severity threshold a stuck pawn's sprite visibly sinks tile by tile toward full submersion and suffocation damage.

rows.section: 3. Excavation as archaeology — better the deeper you dig
rows.label: Stratified tar dig sites
rows.does: Digging deeper costs more time and entrapment risk but yields better loot, up to rare intact, functional ancient machinery.

rows.section: 4a. Canals — tar as a fluid you can move
rows.label: Diggable tar canals
rows.does: Players dig channels that slowly flood tar into a chosen trench, drawing down a finite per-pit reservoir rather than an infinite lever.

rows.section: 4c. Flood-and-ignite, and why it beats grass fire
rows.label: Weaponized slow-burn tar fire
rows.does: Flooded and lit on the player's schedule, tar burns long and smoky, screening sightlines rather than killing outright.

rows.section: 4b. Tar moats — passive base defense
rows.label: Tar moat base defense
rows.does: A canal-fed ring becomes passive base defense — raiders eat the entrapment roll, while a defender who mapped it paths around freely.

rows.section: 5. Tar creatures — what lives in it, and why it's there at all
rows.label: Dormant tar creatures
rows.does: A hidden secretor organism refills drained pits over time, while camouflaged ambush predators strike when a pawn's weight breaks the crust.
rows.invented: A subterranean organism that excretes tar as digestive waste (explaining tar's origin and renewability) — the geology doc establishes the deposit, not a biological source.

rows.section: 6. The horror register — something big, preserved mid-struggle
rows.label: Tar geyser eruption event
rows.does: A cheap, frequent one-shot event sprays open tar across a radius and coats caught pawns in filth on any tile.

rows.section: 6. The horror register — something big, preserved mid-struggle
rows.label: The pit wakes set-piece
rows.does: A rare, expensive deep-dig incident disturbs something reading as freshly dead, triggering a large ambush emergence shaped like an Ancient Danger encounter.

rows.section: 7. Economic uses — tar as a resource, not just a hazard
rows.label: Tar-to-chemfuel refinery chain
rows.does: Tar refined through a pipe network becomes a third fuel path, priced by entrapment risk and dig time, not distance or cold.

docs.title: Propane & Gas Hazard System
docs.oneLine: A pipe/vent/lake propane system where gas density itself is the hazard — turning combat, fuel economy, and heists around a saturation meter.

rows.section: 2. The nightside liquid propane sea — the late-game expedition target
rows.label: Nightside propane sea
rows.does: A late-game tanker destination: harvest the planet's single biggest fuel deposit, but lakeside camps risk ignition and cold kills alike.

rows.section: 3. Gas vents on normal maps — the small, frequent cousin
rows.label: Depletable gas vents
rows.does: Small early hazard/resource: vents periodically puff gas that can self-ignite, capped by CompVentYield so harvesting has a lifespan.

rows.section: 4. PIPE INFRASTRUCTURE — the owner's rupture spark, built out in full
rows.label: Unquenchable pipe rupture jet
rows.does: A ruptured pipe spawns a jet fire that never stops burning until you fight to a distant pump and shut it off.

rows.section: 5. GAS SATURATION as a map condition — the combat-inverting hazard
rows.label: Gas saturation combat inversion
rows.does: Rising gas density makes gunfire risk a fireball on the shooter, forcing melee/stealth/ion tactics instead of guns as saturation climbs.

rows.section: 6. Ship refueling economy — tanker runs
rows.label: Tanker refueling loop
rows.does: One lakeside haul nearly fills the ship's tank in a single trip, but the fuel run home risks igniting your own cargo.

rows.section: 7. Propane-dwelling creatures — why the lake is alive
rows.label: Propane-metabolizing lake creature
rows.does: A submerged predator surfaces when disturbed by pumping or gunfire, fighting you in the most flammable spot on the planet.
rows.invented: invents a hydrocarbon-eating creature as the reason the propane lake stays liquid rather than freezing or evaporating

rows.section: 8. Interplay — fire ecology and tar, tied off explicitly
rows.label: Tar and propane dual hazard
rows.does: An industrial map pipes tar and propane past each other, so a dual rupture blinds you with smoke while a jet burns.

rows.section: 5. GAS SATURATION as a map condition — the combat-inverting hazard
rows.label: Saturation as heist window
rows.does: A saturated depot disarms its own guards from shooting back, turning the hazard into a burglary or smuggling opportunity for the crew.

docs.title: Fire Ecology / The Pyrelands
docs.oneLine: A fire-driven weather loop, four fire-emergent creatures, and harvest windows that make the Pyrelands' burns a place to seek out, not flee.

rows.section: 1. The loop, spelled out as numbers a weather table could hold
rows.label: Pyrelands weather mix
rows.does: No ordinary rain ever falls; thunderstorms hit ~35% of the time so standing grass is always one bad roll from igniting.

rows.section: 1. The loop, spelled out as numbers a weather table could hold
rows.label: Pyroconvective Cell condition
rows.does: A storm cell tracks your own wildfire across the map, boosting lightning strikes near the burn until it runs out of fuel.

rows.section: 3. Fire-only weather — the loop made visible
rows.label: Pyrocumulus regional storm
rows.does: A large fire raises thunderstorm odds map-wide, so the fire that got away can spawn the next storm itself.

rows.section: 2. Fire-emergent creatures — lifecycles that NEED the burn
rows.label: Cinderclutch fire-hatched brood
rows.does: Juveniles boil out of fire-triggered egg clusters mid-burn, feeding on insects the fire flushes out — proof the ecosystem wants the burn.
rows.invented: Invents the Cinderclutch species — fire-resistant eggs that hatch only at ignition temperature.

rows.section: 2. Fire-emergent creatures — lifecycles that NEED the burn
rows.label: Silhouette-hunter firelight predator
rows.does: A predator hunts by firelight and grows more dangerous the bigger your fire gets, punishing colonists who linger near their own blaze.
rows.invented: Invents the Silhouette-hunter predator that hunts by firelight instead of scent or sight.

rows.section: 2. Fire-emergent creatures — lifecycles that NEED the burn
rows.label: Ember-swarm drifting ignition cloud
rows.does: An unkillable ember cloud drifts downwind of a fire and ignites anything flammable it crosses, spreading the burn beyond your control.
rows.invented: Invents the Ember-swarm as a weather-linked 'creature' (a VAST-tier world object, not a pawn kind).

rows.section: 2. Fire-emergent creatures — lifecycles that NEED the burn
rows.label: Slagback walking-hearth megafauna
rows.does: A megafauna grazer permanently smolders and ignites grass wherever it rests, turning its resting spots into deliberate hazards worth escorting or hunting.
rows.invented: Invents the Slagback, a megafauna that permanently smolders and functions as a living hearth.

rows.section: 3. Fire-only weather — the loop made visible
rows.label: Ash ladder and Black Rain
rows.does: Ash builds in four stages that slow movement and choke plants; only a rare Black Rain storm actually extinguishes a large fire.

rows.section: 4. Reasons to be there — harvest windows and drop-ins
rows.label: Scorch-fruit ignition harvest
rows.does: The map's best harvest only opens during or right after a burn, forcing a walk into the fire itself for the payoff.

rows.section: 5. The Deep Desert Tribes as observable fire-farmers
rows.label: Tribes as observable fire-farmers
rows.does: The Tribes visibly set deliberate burn lines, and a player's fire crossing into their territory reads as an act of war.

docs.title: Environmental Ship Shields
docs.oneLine: Gravship modules that gate access to hazardous terrain by holding a survivable bubble around the ship, not by making it harder to kill.

rows.section: 2a. Thermal veil — for the Pyrelands' standing burn
rows.label: Thermal veil module
rows.does: Lets the ship sit near active fire or volcanic tiles instead of cooking; heavy continuous chemfuel draw, hull radiator raiders can target.

rows.section: 2b. Cryo envelope — for the nightside and the propane sea
rows.label: Cryo envelope module
rows.does: Crossing the nightside terminator becomes survivable instead of a death sentence; a heavy fuel spike per activation makes trips expedition-shaped, not casual hops.

rows.section: 2c. Particulate screen — for the deep dust
rows.label: Particulate screen module
rows.does: Dust-storm biomes stop grinding down thrusters and joints; cheapest shield, paid in steel/component maintenance over time rather than fuel, no dramatic failure.

rows.section: 2d. Spore membrane — for the ocular forest headwaters (maybe)
rows.label: Spore membrane module
rows.does: Makes the horror-coded ocular forest enterable by filtering spores from crew air; costliest shield, unlocked via story contact, not bought with research.
rows.invented: Ties the spore membrane's unlock specifically to a Memory Core / Ascendant Helix contact story beat — a new acquisition path this doc proposes, not one prior docs specify.

rows.section: 3. The decision texture — limited hull space, real loadout choices
rows.label: Per-expedition loadout choice
rows.does: Four shields don't fit the ship's hull/power budget at once, forcing a pre-expedition loadout choice, like packing a caravan, not a checkbox.

rows.section: 4. Failure states — the bubble, not a wall
rows.label: Protection bubble, not immunity
rows.does: Shields protect only a radius bubble around the ship; step outside it and the raw hazard applies as if nothing were installed.

rows.section: 4. Failure states — the bubble, not a wall
rows.label: Telegraphed collapse, evacuate beat
rows.does: Running out of fuel or losing the emitter starts a telegraphed countdown before the bubble drops, pushing you to evacuate, not die.

rows.section: 6. How map entry checks the requirement — diegetically, not a hard wall
rows.label: No hard landing wall
rows.does: Landing on an unshielded hazard tile isn't refused: a warning letter first, then full-strength damage ticks immediately if you stay.

docs.title: Water Economy & Heist System
docs.oneLine: Water is the desert's real currency: two-tier potable/non-potable resource, claim-anchored settlements, a heist verb with lasting consequences, guardian creatures, and rain-as-event diplomacy.

rows.section: 0. The two-tier water model
rows.label: Potable/non-potable fork
rows.does: Water reads as a binary at a glance—drinkable or worthless-until-processed—no percentage meter, legible from color/smell/inspect string alone.

rows.section: The detox chain (turns non-potable into potable, at a price)
rows.label: Three-tier detox chain
rows.does: Player chooses cheap-slow crude still, stolen/traded membrane filtration, or wait-it-out spore detox to turn worthless water into wealth.

rows.section: 1. Settlements are built AROUND their water
rows.label: Water-anchored district layout
rows.does: Every settlement radiates outward from its well; the water tile is the single highest, never-decaying claim on the map, drawing defenders there.

rows.section: 2. THE WATER HEIST — the headline capability
rows.label: Deployable hose heist gizmo
rows.does: Player pumps a rival's water into ship tanks under time pressure—faster/greedier pumping is louder and draws witnesses and patrols mid-theft.

rows.section: Persistent consequence: the aquifer remembers
rows.label: Persistent aquifer depletion
rows.does: Draining a water source past a threshold rations or empties it: NPCs migrate, security tightens, a witnessed theft can trigger a bounty.
rows.invented: Invents that a fully drained aquifer becomes a literal cavern entrance, cross-linking to another doc's 'dry cistern shaft' vocabulary.

rows.section: 3. Pool guardians — why every pool survives
rows.label: Dormant pool guardian creatures
rows.does: Small unguarded pools stay safe to hand-draw from but wake a hostile creature under sustained pumping; raiding an oasis needs a plan.
rows.invented: Invents that every pool, however small, hosts a dormant creature/symbiote that explains why undefended water sources aren't already stripped dry.

rows.section: 4. Water diplomacy
rows.label: Drought pricing, tribute, debt-bondage
rows.does: Selling water in a rationed settlement commands a steep markup, threatened settlements pay tribute, and defaulters fall into water-debt bondage.

rows.section: 5. Rain as an event — once a year, everyone stops
rows.label: Rain-as-truce incident
rows.does: Once-a-year rain triggers a collection frenzy and a temporary hostility truce, letting rival factions share open water without fighting.

docs.title: Underground caverns / dungeon-chain design
docs.oneLine: Ship-excluded, chain-of-generated-maps dungeon system giving Ash'karr a secrecy layer the gravship can never reach.

rows.section: 1. THE SHIP STAYS ON THE SURFACE — the design's soul
rows.label: Gravship banned underground
rows.does: No gravship, shields, or ship guns in any cavern map — every underground fight is fought with only what the away team carried down.

rows.section: 1. THE SHIP STAYS ON THE SURFACE — the design's soul
rows.label: Expedition loadout layer
rows.does: Player must pack light, air, water/food and rope before descending, with no resupply and no reinforcements once down.

rows.section: 2. Cavern entrances — how you get down there
rows.label: Four entrance types
rows.does: Sinkholes, drained-void tells, dry cistern shafts, and Rakatan bore-tunnels each visually signal what kind of site the player is entering before they step in.

rows.section: 2. Cavern entrances — how you get down there
rows.label: Drained-well opens dungeon
rows.does: Heisting a settlement's aquifer dry (per the water-economy doc) turns its well into a new cavern entrance, making theft carry a geological consequence.

rows.section: 3. Verticality within a flat-map engine — the map-chain approach
rows.label: Chained generated-map descent
rows.does: Each descent loads a new authored map linked only up/down to its neighbors, avoiding the save-instability of true Z-level stacking while still letting players go deeper.

rows.section: 3. Verticality within a flat-map engine — the map-chain approach
rows.label: Persistent per-site layer state
rows.does: A generated layer keeps its looted/collapsed state for the rest of the campaign instead of resetting on each visit.

rows.section: 4. Subterranean ecology, by depth
rows.label: Depth-banded ecology and economy
rows.does: Each layer down gets stranger and more dangerous — fungal pastures, blind bioluminescent fauna, then a walkable aquifer layer that makes surface water scarcity literal underfoot.

rows.section: 5. Underground settlements — who lives down there, and why
rows.label: Three underground faction archetypes
rows.does: Heat-refugee scavengers, water-immune droid enclaves, and an unexplained pre-human presence give each layer a readable inhabitant silhouette without new dialogue systems.

rows.section: 6. Deep vault bases — new archetypes beyond the existing item
rows.label: Seed vault and flooded gallery
rows.does: Adds a non-combat high-value seed archive and a half-submerged swim-or-fight gallery as new dungeon-endgame variants beyond the existing Rakatan vault.

rows.section: 6. Deep vault bases — new archetypes beyond the existing item
rows.label: Living-cavern organism dungeon
rows.does: A whole layer acts as one creature with a shared irritation meter, so disturbing one room raises hazard risk in rooms the player hasn't found yet.
rows.invented: That a cavern layer can be a single distributed living organism spanning rooms with a shared reactive meter — no prior doc establishes this creature.

rows.section: 7. Collapse and cave-in — hazard AND tool
rows.label: Cave-in as hazard and weapon
rows.does: Unstable ceilings threaten the party, but a deliberate collapse lets the player permanently seal off pursuers or open a shortcut between rooms.

rows.section: 8. Darkness as a real mechanic
rows.label: Light-draws-predators system
rows.does: Carrying too much light attracts danger while mastering low light grants quieter passage, inverting the surface's too-much-light problem into a real resource tradeoff.

docs.title: Reign-Modes
docs.oneLine: An escalation layer where an L-tier god boon/curse that goes unresolved becomes a days-long world-changing mode with opportunity, cost, and a permanent scar.

rows.section: 1. Entry — existing thresholds, held
rows.label: Entry thresholds (pleased/angry-lock)
rows.does: A god's existing Exalted/decadence or unpaid-curse threshold silently escalates one L-tier event into a days-long mode instead of a letter.

rows.section: 2. Strain — the mechanism behind "yearning"
rows.label: Strain meter (yearning clock)
rows.does: A hidden 0-100 meter speeds the challenge clock, cheapens exiting over time (floor 40%), and unlocks a cheaper substitute offering past 60.

rows.section: 3. Exit, stacking, memory
rows.label: Exit, stacking, and scars
rows.does: Only one god's mode runs; exit costs its stated price, a cut-off mode scars as broken, and outcomes get recorded.

rows.section: 4. Announcement (F17)
rows.label: Reign-wide announcement layer
rows.does: Entry gets a distinct sting and re-titles every incident letter through the mode's lens; exit gets a calmer, closing sting.

rows.section: 5. The eighteen modes
rows.label: Eighteen paired mode roster
rows.does: Nine gods each get a pleased and angry mode — a GameConditionDef changing 2-3 rules plus opportunity, cost, and exit.

rows.section: 5. The eighteen modes — ④-P Mob'Unloo, "The Open Market"
rows.label: Open Market (trader flood)
rows.does: Trader visits and prices spike in the colony's favor for the mode's span, but displayed wealth scales the raids that follow.

rows.section: 5. The eighteen modes — ⑥-A Ta'Baa, "The Long Walk"
rows.label: Long Walk (sleepwalker)
rows.does: Nightly, one pawn sleepwalks toward the map edge and must be actively chased down or risk exposure, heatstroke, or being lost.

rows.section: Build ladder — Dream
rows.label: Tenfold Reign (dream finale)
rows.does: A hand-authored once-per-campaign finale where all nine gods hit extremity together, reading the whole Reign-Scars ledger back before the last choice.
rows.invented: Names a specific single-fire endgame myth-event, 'the Tenfold Reign,' where every god crosses into extremity simultaneously — not established in prior canon docs.

docs.title: The Skyhook
docs.oneLine: A visitable Imperial skyhook anchor on tidally-locked Ash'karr: fixed shadow, a rigger caste, claimed cargo to steal, and a quest arc to cut the cable.

rows.section: 1. The anchor site as a visitable map
rows.label: Eternal shadow line
rows.does: Gives players a permanently cool, dark, cheaper-to-build-in shade band at fixed map cells, since the sun never moves to shift it.

rows.section: 1. The anchor site as a visitable map
rows.label: Scheduled cargo climber arrivals
rows.does: Replaces a random incident with a felt, timetabled event: ground tremor two minutes out, then a screaming pod delivering cargo to a fixed cell.

rows.section: 1. The anchor site as a visitable map
rows.label: Tether Static weather
rows.does: Adds a rare, telegraphed lightning-strike risk to exposed pawns and structures, geofenced to only trigger near the anchor.

rows.section: 2. What rides the tether
rows.label: Intercept pod cargo mid-flight
rows.does: Shooting or sabotaging a descending pod scatters its still-hot, still-claimed Imperial cargo across the map before customs response arrives.

rows.section: 2. What rides the tether
rows.label: Steal cargo from the customs yard
rows.does: Landed pods sit under high Imperial security, turning theft into a witnessed heist with faction-record consequences instead of a free raid.

rows.section: 3. The vertical society
rows.label: Rigger caste and shrines
rows.does: Gives anchor-town a unique, recruitable/bribeable working population with real grievances, plus folk shrines players can encounter before the Imperial garrison.

rows.section: 4. THE CUT — the campaign set-piece
rows.label: The Cut quest arc
rows.does: Players choose quiet sabotage or loud assault to sever the tether, trading a chance to warn riggers against speed and a Hutt deadline.

rows.section: 4. THE CUT — the campaign set-piece
rows.label: Debris corridor world reveal
rows.does: Cutting the tether permanently unlocks a pre-authored, salvage-rich hazardous world region and lowers Imperial patrol strength region-wide.

rows.section: 5. Smaller exotica
rows.label: Cable-hum prophecy cult
rows.does: Adds a tolerated rigger folk sect whose 'prophecy' quests secretly function as an early-warning system for climbers and weather.
rows.invented: A new non-Jawa folk religious sect built around reading tether vibrations as prophecy, distinct from the Ninefold and Imperial doctrine, not established in any prior lore doc.

docs.title: Ludicrous Livestock — Deep Design
docs.oneLine: Fourteen original creatures across four families whose products are multi-step processes, services, debts, or labor-gated cons — not flat resource printers.

rows.section: 2. INDUSTRIAL GUTS
rows.label: Kiln-belly ceramic batches
rows.does: Feed it in three spaced doses over a day for sellable ceramic; a single cold dump fires cracked, worthless batches instead.

rows.section: 2. INDUSTRIAL GUTS
rows.label: Sorted-alloy smelting glands
rows.does: Produces sorted ingots by alloy class, but mixed unsorted scrap chokes it — no output for days plus a vet event.

rows.section: 3. UTILITY SYMBIOTES
rows.label: Cured molt-plate armor
rows.does: Sheds wearable plate armor every ~15 days, but disturbing the molt turns it aggressive and ruins the shed entirely.

rows.section: 3. UTILITY SYMBIOTES
rows.label: Stored-grief liability bomb
rows.does: Eases a grieving pawn's mood now, but every debuff it absorbs releases back on the whole colony at once when it dies.
rows.invented: An animal that stores absorbed grief debuffs as a hidden liability released catastrophically on death — no precedent in the livestock/pets baseline's four resource-excreters.

rows.section: 3. UTILITY SYMBIOTES
rows.label: Living herd warmth buff
rows.does: A big enough herd sleeping nearby gives a real cold-tile comfort buff, but cannot survive the itinerary's hot legs.

rows.section: 3. UTILITY SYMBIOTES
rows.label: Autonomous power donation
rows.does: Unpenned, it seeks out and tops off the base's least-charged battery on its own — no feeding job required, ever.

rows.section: 4. ABSURD ECONOMY
rows.label: Tend & Narrate milking job
rows.does: Requires a dedicated pawn to sit and tell it stories for the full session, or the milk comes out thin and worthless.

rows.section: 4. ABSURD ECONOMY
rows.label: Silver-eater trade con
rows.does: Excretes near-passable fake silver at a net 20% loss — a Jawa clan sells it to a mark, never keeps one.

rows.section: 5. HERDING DRAMA
rows.label: Aimed weaponized stampede
rows.does: Trigger a trained herd's stampede on command at a target — but a misfire runs it through your own base instead.

rows.section: 5. HERDING DRAMA
rows.label: Undermining siege digger
rows.does: Directed at an enemy wall it slowly collapses the foundation — left unsupervised near your own structures it does the same.

docs.title: High Cuisine & Brewing
docs.oneLine: Cuisine and brewing built as a diplomacy instrument, hazard-sourced pantry, and religious capstone feast, repointing existing cooking mods rather than new content.

rows.section: 4. Ingredient rarity tied to world hazards
rows.label: Hazard-sourced pantry ingredients
rows.does: Four rare ingredients (scorch-fruit, tar-preserved meat, cryo-delicacies, pool-guardian roe) only come from dangerous biomes, giving caravans a reason to risk hazard terrain.
rows.invented: The tidally-locked-world food ecology (scorch-fruit, tar-preserved meat, nightside cryo-delicacies, pool-guardian roe) is this doc's own invention — no Star Wars canon covers it.

rows.section: 5. Dish tiers — Tier 2, the repointed VCE tier
rows.label: Repointed VCE recipe tiers
rows.does: Existing Vanilla Cooking Expanded recipe types (grills, wraps, stews) get reskinned onto Star Wars/hazard ingredients instead of new bespoke dish defs.

rows.section: 3. Meals are statements — cuisine as a diplomacy instrument
rows.label: Meals as diplomacy claims
rows.does: A served dish carries its ingredients' theft history; disclosing a stolen delicacy is a boast, hiding it risks faction-level incidents on discovery.
rows.invented: A serve-the-correct-or-humiliating-delicacy-to-an-envoy ritual is this doc's own extrapolation — the compendium documents a status-food category, not this specific scene.

rows.section: 5. Dish tiers — Tier 4, the Nine-Course Ninefold Feast
rows.label: Nine-Course Ninefold Feast ritual
rows.does: A nine-course ritual meal, one course per god, gives no material reward — only mood, narrative, and ritual-participation eligibility.

rows.section: 6.1 Fermentation — the terminator's one clear advantage
rows.label: Terminator-belt fermentation terroir
rows.does: Fermentation quality only peaks in the terminator zone, turning that strip of desert into territory worth holding or fighting for.

rows.section: 7. Cooking as performance
rows.label: Chef role and banquet service
rows.does: An emergent chef identity and a reskinned waiter job make banquet success depend on service and presentation, with room-wide mood effects.

rows.section: 8. Recipe discovery — recipes as loot, rumor, and quest reward
rows.label: Recipes as loot/rumor rewards
rows.does: Recipes aren't researched — they're found as stolen cookbooks, rumors, or district-visit rewards, replacing a tech tree with treasure-hunting.

rows.section: 9. Food preservation vocabulary for a desert
rows.label: Salt-crust, tar-seal, sand-oven preservation
rows.does: Three desert-native preservation methods — salt-crust, tar-seal, sand-oven — give cheap hazard-themed alternatives to canning, one sharing cookware with the livestock doc.

rows.section: Build ladder — Dream
rows.label: Live-ingredient tank (aquaculture)
rows.does: A tank of live aquatic creatures yields an eaten-alive delicacy — the one piece needing real new C#.

docs.title: The Oracle — Sparse LLM Consumers
docs.oneLine: A shared LLM client (the Oracle) powers several rare, validated text/menu consumers -- droid translation, god rites, rumors, recap letters -- never touching game state directly.

rows.section: 2. Protocol-droid interpreters — a voice for the thing that has none
rows.label: Protocol droid translation voice
rows.does: First contact or a captured alien's dying words get one flavored translation, filtered through that droid's own quirky personality; rejection yields a funnier stock line.

rows.section: 3. The Nine Voices, through the shrine — one call per rite, never a chat window
rows.label: Shrine rite god dialogue
rows.does: A shrine rite's LLM payoff fires only after mechanics already decided success or failure; one of nine gods speaks in character, C# picks who.

rows.section: 3. The Nine Voices, through the shrine — one call per rite, never a chat window
rows.label: Shared 3-calls-per-day cap
rows.does: Nine gods share one pool of 3 LLM calls per in-game day rather than per-god allowances; exceeding it silently ships the prescripted fragment, no visible cap.

rows.section: 4. Inhabited rumor dialogue — the barkeep knows what the town knows, because the fabric already tracked it
rows.label: Cast pawn rumor lines
rows.does: Talking to a cast pawn surfaces their actual hidden knowledge as one cached, in-character rumor line; nothing invented beyond what the perception fabric recorded.

rows.section: 4. Inhabited rumor dialogue — the barkeep knows what the town knows, because the fabric already tracked it
rows.label: Player-name injection fencing
rows.does: Player-set colonist and item names get fenced as inert data in the prompt, so even a successful injection can only produce rejected out-of-character text.

rows.section: 5. Letters and quest text, written from what actually happened
rows.label: Session recap and goals letter
rows.does: Loading a save gets one recap letter plus session goals drawn from last session's real events; the cheapest cadence in the whole roster, once per load.

rows.section: 5. Letters and quest text, written from what actually happened
rows.label: Salvaged item provenance text
rows.does: A rare item found in-world gets a name and two-line history picked from a fixed trait vocabulary; mechanical stats it already rolled never change.

rows.section: 5. Letters and quest text, written from what actually happened
rows.label: Quest resolution consequence flags
rows.does: Quest resolution can add a goodwill delta, rumor-spread flag, or resentment flag chosen from a clamped legal menu — the one consumer here that touches faction numbers.

rows.section: 6. Failure design — what the player actually sees when it breaks
rows.label: Uniform silent-fallback failure mode
rows.does: Every failure (timeout, bad output, budget hit, kill-switch off) looks identical to the player: the pre-written fallback ships with zero visible AI trace, ever.

docs.title: Terminator Weather Suite
docs.oneLine: Eight tidally-locked weather systems — terminator storms, static seasons, pressure tides, auroras, spore blooms, mirages — placed as fixed WeatherDefs/GameConditionDefs, no worldgen, on the frozen Ash'karr map.

rows.section: 1. Terminator storms — the permanent front you fly through, not around
rows.label: Terminator Front Crossing
rows.does: Every gravship flight crosses the terminator's permanent storm wall — navigation penalty, mishap risk, electronics hazard, but free condensed water there too.

rows.section: 2. Glass-sand storms — beautiful, lethal, and worth harvesting afterward
rows.label: Glass Storm + Fulgurite Harvest
rows.does: Rare storms inflict shrapnel wounds, foul solar power, boost wind power, then leave harvestable glass nodes on the ground afterward.
rows.invented: Fulgurite glass-node harvest as a new post-storm resource; full storm lethality (vs. vanilla's cosmetic-wear glass storms) is an invented escalation.

rows.section: 3. Static seasons — weeks where everything metal bites
rows.label: Static Season Buildup
rows.does: Weeks-long electrical buildup causes shocks, battery drain, shorter comms range, and droid coherence disruption, sometimes escalating into a glass storm.
rows.invented: The causal chain linking terminator-front charge separation to static seasons to glass storms is invented connective physics, not established in prior docs.

rows.section: 4. The great pressure tides — wind you can set a calendar by
rows.label: Pressure Tide Wind Cycle
rows.does: A slow planet-wide wind cycle rewards players who time gravship launches and wind-rig hauling for the tailwind phase.
rows.invented: The planet-scale oscillating 'pressure tide' (a weeks-long sloshing wind cycle) is a new planetary mechanic beyond what the tidally-locked-world doctrine established.

rows.section: 5. Dark-side auroras — the one beauty the night side owns
rows.label: Dark-Side Aurora
rows.does: The only zero-cost nightside event — a free mood buff and partial sight-range restoration in the otherwise punishing dark hemisphere.
rows.invented: A magnetospheric aurora driven by the planet's electrical activity is a new lore premise, not established by the tidal-lock doctrine.

rows.section: 6. Spore blooms off the ocular forests — beauty that is also the R-H7 poison, airborne
rows.label: Spore Bloom Haze
rows.does: Rare toxic haze drifts downwind of the ocular forests, poisoning pawns near-source but leaving a short-lived forageable bonus once it passes.
rows.invented: The R-H7 doc established the ocular forests' toxin vapor; this doc invents the airborne bloom weather event and its post-bloom plant-growth-bonus tile as new content.

rows.section: 7. Mirage events — did you SEE that?
rows.label: Mirage / False Sighting
rows.does: False oases and phantom caravans waste travel time and heat exposure, and can seed a false rumor into the gossip network.
rows.invented: Tying mirages to the perception fabric so a false sighting seeds a real (but fabricated) witnessed-event rumor is an invented mechanic, unconfirmed against the fabric's actual schema.

rows.section: 8. Forecasting as wealth — a tech ladder for a world that punishes ignorance
rows.label: Forecasting Tech Ladder
rows.does: A five-tier building ladder, folk signs to orbital meteorology, turns every other weather system into a planned advantage instead of a surprise.

docs.title: The Sarlacc — Deep Design
docs.oneLine: A single fixed, hand-placed sarlacc pit landmark on Ash'karr with disposal/tribute/evidence economy, tremor-based danger, and one sanctioned Anomaly-toolbox reuse.

rows.section: The pit as a permanent authored map feature
rows.label: Fixed pit landmark
rows.does: One sarlacc, placed once on the frozen map forever — reads as visibly wrong at a glance long before it's dangerous, never a random spawn.

rows.section: The multi-decade digestion fiction
rows.label: Compile, not dissolve
rows.does: Nothing eaten is truly gone — bodies, evidence, and minds are absorbed and can resurface decades later; rescues never come back unchanged.
rows.invented: Invents 'digestion as compile' biology: the sarlacc retains and reuses everything it eats, including fragments of consumed minds, indefinitely.

rows.section: Feeding the pit — disposal, tribute, and the ownership fabric
rows.label: Feed it your evidence
rows.does: Feeding stolen goods or evidence into the pit erases the claim now, but it can resurface decades later as a mineralized clue for someone new.

rows.section: Tremor-sense — walk softly
rows.label: Disturbance/tremor gating
rows.does: Running, gunfire, and machinery raise a shared disturbance reading near the pit; staying quiet lowers strike risk, with visible tells before an attack.

rows.section: Anomaly-toolbox draws — used, not laundered
rows.label: Anomaly verb reuse
rows.does: Sarlacc reuses Anomaly's grab-and-drag verb, off-map threat presence, and rim-only terrain corruption — the one creature in the campaign allowed to touch that toolbox.

rows.section: The escape quest — someone climbs out
rows.label: Rescue-from-the-pit quest
rows.does: A rare, rumor-driven quest lets a player rescue someone alive inside the sarlacc, but the survivor comes back permanently changed, never a free recruit.

rows.section: Spawn and lifecycle horror — the sky-seeding myth
rows.label: Sky-seeding folklore
rows.does: Jawa folklore hints the sarlacc fell from the sky decades ago, but it's never confirmed and never produces a second pit anywhere on the map.
rows.invented: Invents a specific 'fell from the sky' origin myth for this sarlacc, beyond canon's deliberately vague spread mechanism.

rows.section: Economy — castings as a unique material
rows.label: Casting biomineral material
rows.does: Cutting open a shed casting yields a unique craft material and sometimes a recognizable relic; killing the sarlacc for it yields worse quality than patient harvesting.
rows.invented: Invents 'castings' — indigestible cores the sarlacc coats in biomineral layers over years, sometimes preserving recognizable evidence at the center.

rows.section: Cross-cite — the sarlacc's roots, underground
rows.label: Root-system cavern merge
rows.does: The pit's underground root tissue could literally become the caverns doc's 'living cavern' dream feature, sharing one disturbance meter, if both owners agree to merge.

docs.title: SW Mod Concepts Triage
docs.oneLine: A triage of 28 candidate Star Wars mod concepts against existing campaign docs and canon, with 7 taken to full expanded mini-designs.

rows.section: A. Junk Is Civilization — provenance and the scrap-built weapon tier
rows.label: Salvage Provenance & Scrap Weapons
rows.does: Salvage remembers where it came from — recognized gear sparks haggling or theft trouble later, and rare pieces hide a surprise capability.

rows.section: B. Krayt Leviathans — sand as an ocean, pearls as its pearl
rows.label: Krayt Leviathans, Sand Ocean
rows.does: A sandworm-scale creature roams as a weather event with its own music; killing it yields loot, riding its wake yields rarer pearls.
rows.invented: Krayt dragons reimagined as sand-swimming, migratory 'leviathan' world-objects (a Dune-style sandworm register) rather than canon's stationary reptilian desert predators.

rows.section: C. Galactic Underworld Reputation — debts outlive the fight
rows.label: Underworld Debt Ledger
rows.does: Owing a faction becomes its own lasting state, separate from war — unpaid debts, ambiguous Hutt contracts, and bounty hunters return later.

rows.section: D. The Cantina, socially — rumors, gambling, and a stage
rows.label: Cantina Rumors & Music
rows.does: Cantina rumors and maps can simply be wrong, sending caravans chasing bad leads; music and reputation play out at the tables.

rows.section: E. Holo-Deception — projection as a weapon, a wall, and a lie
rows.label: Holographic Deception & Traps
rows.does: Fake floors and false walls hide real hazards or capture traps, readable only by species-specific detection, giving non-lethal capture and cheap defense.

rows.section: F. Imperial Bureaucracy — the Empire that doesn't have to fight you
rows.label: Imperial Inspections & Bureaucracy
rows.does: Imperial patrols inspect one narrow thing and the colony is rarely clean; comply, forge, bribe, hide, or refuse, each with real cost.

rows.section: G. Droid Behavior & the Repair Shop — the tail Droidworks left open
rows.label: Droid Chassis Personality & Repair Shop
rows.does: Droid chassis type biases personality — a protocol droid can worsen negotiations through pedantic honesty — and repair-shop visitors sometimes hide dangerous surprises.
